canonicalFacts.claim: Triptans are first-line treatments for moderate to severe migraines
Acetaminophen and NSAIDs are first-line treatments for mild to moderate migraines
CGRP receptor antagonists (gepants) represent a new class of acute migraine treatment
Topiramate, botulinum toxin type A, and CGRP monoclonal antibodies are effective for chronic migraine with medication overuse headache
Zavegepant nasal spray is effective for acute migraine treatment

redFlags: Triptans may be expensive despite effectiveness
Maximum acute treatment is associated with reduced risk of transformation from episodic to chronic migraine

excludedAgents.name: probiotic and vitamin D co-supplementation
excludedAgents.reason: randomized controlled trial found no significant improvement in migraine clinical symptoms, mental health, or inflammation markers

excludedAgents.name: eicosapentaenoic acid
excludedAgents.reason: randomized controlled trial of daily 2000 mg EPA supplementation showed no efficacy in chronic migraine management

excludedAgents.name: atorvastatin
excludedAgents.reason: randomized controlled trial found no preventive effect when combined with nortriptyline for migraine-type headache

excludedAgents.name: inulin
excludedAgents.reason: randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial showed no effect on migraine headache characteristics, quality of life, or mental health symptoms

excludedAgents.name: thiamine
excludedAgents.reason: randomized controlled trial of high-dose thiamine showed no improvement in migraine headache characteristics in women with episodic migraine
